concepts.why: The presence of an intraepidermal neoplasm with pagetoid cells and positive staining for CK7 and EMA supports this diagnosis.
The presence of numerous reactive dendritic HMB-45–positive melanocytes scattered among tumor cells suggests a melanocytic origin.
The initial presentation of a small eczematous, pink-to-brown plaque and the subsequent change in color to dark brown is consistent with this diagnosis.
The presence of an enlarged and variegated plaque with well-demarcated margins is consistent with this diagnosis.

The presence of numerous reactive dendritic HMB-45–positive melanocytes scattered among tumor cells and the intraepidermal neoplasm with pagetoid cells suggests a melanocytic origin and possible malignancy.
The presence of pagetoid cells with round, pale vacuolated cytoplasm and large pleomorphic nuclei is a characteristic finding in pagetoid melanocytic proliferation.
